clue.text: Novel from China we share

definitions.meaning: a Dickens novel, his last completed one
china is rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for a pal, so one we share is a pal common to us both

explanation.surface: A book imported from China that we are passing round between us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links the two definitions. China is Cockney rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with 'mate', so a china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's final completed novel carries this title, and a friend common to us both is described by the same phrase.

clue.text: Plump mother holding one in top condition

parts.note: to plump for something is to opt for it
I is the Roman numeral for one
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A stout mother clutches one child, both in the best of health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump' looks like 'fat' but is the verb 'choose'. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the best or most favourable state, so top condition.

clue.text: Drivers try to steer clear of this hooligan

definitions.text: Drivers try to steer clear of this
definitions.meaning: golfers hitting drives try to keep out of the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.definitionFit: In golf the long grass beside the fairway is avoided by drivers, and a thug is called by the same word.

clue.text: Lear's ancient relative? Not obviously

definitions.meaning: Edward Lear wrote a poem about the old wanderer 'My ...'
in an unclear way, without being plain

explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear's poem concerns an aged Uncle Arly, and the same letters form an adverb meaning in a way that is not clear.

clue.text: Not fresh, and oddly unsteady

indicators.note: take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tired thing, and strangely wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something second-hand or already worn is not fresh.

clue.text: Knight involved in mating combination with queen

definitions.text: Knight involved in mating combination with queen

parts.words: Knight involved in mating combination with queen
parts.note: reads like a chess move where a knight and queen deliver checkmate, but describes the Round Table knight who had an affair with Arthur's queen, Guinevere

explanation.definitionFit: The Arthurian knight famously had a love affair with Queen Guinevere, a mating combination of a different kind.

clue.text: Tree's weight borne by horse

indicators.note: the weight letter is carried inside the animal word

parts.note: a roan is a horse with a coat of mixed colour

explanation.surface: A horse carrying the weight of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The rowan, or mountain ash, is a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Lovingly running off work framed in gold, say

indicators.note: the work word is set inside the chemical word like a picture in a frame

parts.note: gold is an example of a chemical element
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: An artwork set in a gilt frame is admired fondly as someone walks off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gold, say' wants to be OR, the heraldic gold, but 'say' marks an example: gold is an ELEMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is running away secretly to marry, so a running off for love.

clue.text: With fingers, but without hands

definitions.meaning: relating to the fingers, the digits
a watch showing numbers on a display rather than hands

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to fingers, and a clock with a numeric display rather than hands is described the same way.

clue.text: Get time right for start of meal in club

indicators.note: one thing put in place of the first letter of another: here the opening letter of the meal word gives way

parts.note: luncheon is a formal midday meal

explanation.surface: Instructions to arrive on time for the first course at a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get' is a link. T and R replace L, the first letter of LUNCHEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy stick carried by police, a type of club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Grown like this, it's bad

indicators.note: the letters are to be arranged in the manner the answer itself describes, that is, all awry

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A remark that something grown in this shape is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself the anagram signal: GROWN arranged 'like this' means arranged badly. 'it's' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorrect or morally faulty is bad, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Composer Lehar confused with Mozart, initially

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the composer's name named after it is wanted
the operetta composer's name is jumbled into a new order

parts.note: Franz Lehár, composer of The Merry Widow, his name taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muddles up the operetta composer Lehár with Mozart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' is the anagram signal and 'initially' takes just the opening letter of Mozart; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer of symphonies and songs.

clue.text: Control horse, check about direction, and plough back

parts.note: to rein in a horse is to control it, so the verb here is rein

indicators.note: the examining word goes around the compass point

parts.note: to vet something is to check it over
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Riding instructions: hold back the horse, get it examined, and plough the field again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts S inside VET to make VEST. 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To plough back profits is to put them into the business again, an idiom for investing them anew.

clue.text: What I would give to guarantee goodness!

definitions.text: What I would give to guarantee
definitions.meaning: giving one's promise, one's solemn pledge, guarantees something
an exclamation of surprise, like 'well I never!'

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a personal pledge offered as a guarantee and an old-fashioned cry of surprise.

clue.text: Mixed drink including sack -— why I'm drunk?

indicators.note: being drunk, these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they are tipsy after a cocktail laced with sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' is a link. Sack is an old word for sherry, which adds to the boozy picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A whisky mac is a mixed drink of whisky and ginger wine.

clue.text: Cheat with scoundrel, one engaged with others in revolution

definitions.text: one engaged with others in revolution

parts.note: to cog is an old word for cheating, especially loading dice
a heel is a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A con artist teams up with a villain, as one of several conspirators in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests political uprising but means turning; 'engaged' is in the gearing sense of teeth meshing.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed wheel meshes with other gears as they turn, so it is engaged with others while rotating.

clue.text: Moral justification for hard labour

parts.note: sounds like a penal argument for sentencing prisoners, but describes the principle that diligent toil is virtuous

explanation.definitionFit: The belief that hard work has moral value is exactly a principle justifying toil.

clue.text: Man's in this main area

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man, and the main is the sea, so this is the stretch of sea where that island lies

explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man sits in the stretch of sea between Great Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: One holds up canvas showing old woman outside house

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one's old woman
the yard is the ground outside a house, so outdoors there you are in the yard

explanation.surface: A painting depicts an elderly lady standing outside her home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canvas' suggests a painting but means sails. 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sailing ship the yard on the mainmast supports the mainsail, so it holds up sailcloth.

clue.text: Economist is following a founder of brotherhood

indicators.note: the word is comes after the a in the answer

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a philosopher and economist

explanation.surface: A remark that an economist follows a man who founded a fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: The brotherhood is the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood of painters, founded in 1848 by Millais, Rossetti and Holman Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: John Everett Millais was one of the three painters who founded the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: Introduction takes short time, not indefinitely extended

indicators.note: the preface word takes the time letter into itself

parts.note: a proem is a preface or introduction
T is the shortened form of time

explanation.surface: A preface that only takes a moment, not one that goes on for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means for the time being, that is, temporary rather than lasting indefinitely.

clue.text: Damage NATO member with cut in terms of alliance

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: the country's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Italy is a member of the NATO alliance

explanation.surface: Harming a NATO country by slashing its share of the alliance's budget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes Y, leaving ITAL. 'with' is a link. 'alliance' suggests NATO but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to marriage, which is an alliance between spouses.

clue.text: Preference is held by partners, also

parts.note: a liking or like is a preference

indicators.note: the little word sits inside the pair of players

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at bridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple both hold the same preference too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' is the container signal. In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, with East and West partnering each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means in the same way or too, a synonym of also.

clue.text: Add extra to one direction

parts.note: in cricket a wide is an extra, a run given for a ball bowled out of reach
N, north, is one compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions to tack on a bit more in a particular direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. In cricket, runs not scored off the bat are extras, and a wide is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen something is to add to its breadth, broadening it.

clue.text: Bird, blithe spirit when aloft?

definitions.meaning: keeping one's courage up means staying cheerful, so this spirit is blithe when held high

explanation.definitionFit: A woodpecker is often called by this shorter name, and 'keep your pecker up' is British slang for staying cheerful.

clue.text: Move to South of Eastern capital, a nearby city

indicators.note: the little word printed next is shifted elsewhere within the capital's name
in a down answer, to the south means lower down, so to the bottom

parts.note: Tokyo is the capital of Japan in the East
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to relocate south of a Far Eastern capital, to a city close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is both a word in the instruction and the letters moved: TO goes from the top of TOKYO to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto, the old imperial capital, is a Japanese city not far from Tokyo by Japanese standards.

clue.text: A dozen — should be just enough for a case

definitions.text: A dozen — should be just enough for a case

parts.words: A dozen — should be just enough for a case
parts.note: twelve people needed for a court trial, who ought to be fair, rather than twelve items filling a box

explanation.definitionFit: A trial jury has twelve members who should give a just verdict in a legal case.

clue.text: Prepared for battle — Nelson became singularly so

definitions.meaning: Admiral Nelson lost his right arm in 1797 and was left with a single one

explanation.definitionFit: Carrying weapons means ready for war, and Nelson after losing an arm was one-armed.

clue.text: A mile out of Portsmouth, reversed into seaside resort

indicators.note: the two halves of what is left change places, the front part going to the end
the distance letter is taken away from the naval port's name

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mile

explanation.surface: Someone drives a mile out of Portsmouth and then backs into a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes M, leaving PORTSOUTH; 'reversed' swaps the two halves, putting PORT after SOUTH. 'into' is a link. Southport is a resort on the coast of Merseyside.
explanation.definitionFit: Southport is a seaside resort town on the Lancashire and Merseyside coast in north-west England.

clue.text: Where youth's instructed to transfer fish on a railway

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece on another follows it

parts.note: to second someone is to transfer them temporarily to another post
a school is a group of fish swimming together

explanation.surface: Instructions to move fish along a railway line, given to young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' looks like moving the fish but means to second someone to another post; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondary school is where young people are taught after primary level, a place of instruction for youth.
